text:
Maria: FYI I ran a perf pass on the private VPC stack this morning — saw a tail latency regression on a few customer routes after the kernel-selector change.
Dennis: ugh, which kernel change? the AVX2->TVM fused kernels we rolled last week?
Maria: Yeah. On paper the new kernel lowers median but increases p99 for long sequences. KV cache hit paths seem fine, but token-level latency histograms show a small but consistent bump in the 200-500ms bin for cached requests.
Oliver: Can you paste the profiling snippet? wondering if it's batching or KV serialization noise.
Maria: Here are the snippets from perf-trace for route /v1/generate (quantized model):
```
kernel_selector_choice{kernel="fused_tvm_v2",seq_len="512",model="mosaic-qlo"} 1
inference_kernel_latency_ms_bucket{le="10"} 1200
inference_kernel_latency_ms_bucket{le="100"} 4200
inference_kernel_latency_ms_bucket{le="500"} 5120
kv_cache_hit_ratio{route="/v1/generate"} 0.94
inference_batch_size{route="/v1/generate"} 1
```
Anya: Looks like a lot of single-item batches hitting the fused kernel. We expected fused_tvm_v2 to be better at small batches, but maybe it degrades with kv cache continuation (lots of cache restores).
Dennis: Could be the kernel's memory access pattern — when KV restore crosses a page boundary it flushes and that is expensive. We saw something similar in 176... tickets.
Maria: Agree. I'm thinking we need token-level instrumentation in the private export so customers can see 'token_expand' vs 'kv_restore' latency breakdown. Right now our export only has inference_token_latency_seconds and aggregate labels.
Oliver: For VPC customers we also need to support air-gapped metrics export. Two proposals:
- Sidecar relay that writes periodic samples to a mounted S3/MinIO bucket (customer pulls), plus local prometheus file_sd tarball.
- Pushgateway-like secure agent that does authenticated remote_write to the customer's Prometheus when egress allowed.
Anya: Sidecar + file_sd seems safest for fully air-gapped. We should include a manifest generator that creates a set of metric descriptors and label conventions customers can import into Grafana.
Maria: For immediate debugging I'm pushing a patch to add these labels:
- kernel_version
- kernel_fallback (true/false)
- batch_window_ms
- kv_restore_time_ms
- token_phase (prefix|generation|kv_restore)
Dennis: Nice. Add route and model_version labels too. Also ensure cardinality stays bounded: kernel_version should be normalized to a short hash.
perf-bot: Automated trace: route=/v1/generate p50=18ms p95=120ms p99=390ms kv_hit=0.94 kernel=fused_tvm_v2 batch=1
Oliver: We should also expose per-route KPIs in our Grafana provisioning: per_route_qps, per_route_token_cost, per_route_p95_latency and a stacked bar for token-level breakdown. That will help Product and SRE triage customer tickets quickly.
Maria: Agreed. For the VPC prometheus scrape we need to add relabeling so that customer-internal metrics don't leak internal tags. Sample relabel config I'm testing:
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app]
    regex: redwood-inference
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [instance]
    target_label: instance
    replacement: "${POD_IP}"
```
Dennis: Also add a filter to drop dense histogram buckets for internal debug unless debug_export=true on the config. Otherwise file_sd tarballs get huge.
Anya: For Grafana provisioning: create dashboards with variables: customer_id, route, kernel_version. Use recording rules for per_route_token_rate and per_route_kv_miss_rate so dashboards are cheap.
Maria: I've opened a PR with instrumentation changes and a proposal doc for the sidecar file export. Tests: local e2e with a simulated air-gap (no egress) + prometheus running in the same vnet. Early run shows p99 reduced by ~50ms when forcing fallback to scalar kernel (slower median but better tail) — so dynamic kernel fallback might be the right short-term mitigation.
Oliver: Important: the private control plane needs to enable toggle for auto-fallback per-customer. Can't be global.
Dennis: Ops note: ensure the sidecar signs the bundle with customer key so they can validate. Also we need retention and rotation policy for stored metric bundles on the node.
Maria: I'll add a telemetry flag to surface when kernel_fallback=true so we can correlate customer incidents.
perf-bot: Regression alert created for customer=acme-corp route=/v1/generate threshold=p99>350ms
Anya: Next steps: Maria will land the labels + recording rules. Oliver will prototype the sidecar exporter. Dennis will add kernel telemetry to the runtime and a bounded label sanitizer. I'll make Grafana dashboard templates and provisioning snippets.
Maria: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link in this thread once it's up. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy job queued for branch/infra/vpc-metrics (no egress changes)
